dual_deadlines.hw_secondary_due: Review responses (Step 3) due before Week 12 Meeting 1
dual_deadlines.description: The main W10 homework (peer review document and ethics statement) is due before Week 11 Meeting 1. However, Step 3 — responding to the partner's review of YOUR code — is due a full week later, before Week 12 Meeting 1. This secondary deadline is stated at the bottom of Step 3 in the instructions and is repeated in the top-level 'due' field as a second clause: 'Peer review submitted before Week 11 Meeting 1; review responses due before Week 12 Meeting 1'.
dual_deadlines.student_impact: Students may not realize there is a delayed component that extends one full week past the assignment's headline due date. The review-response step is graded as part of the W12 homework (HW Step 2), not W10, which makes the dependency easy to miss. Missing the W12 deadline means failing a graded criterion of the W12 submission.

assessment_milestones.note: Weeks 6, 7, 8, 9, and 13 all carry assessment_category 'Final Project Codebase & Paper'. None of these weeks have an independent numeric grade — their deliverables are components of the final repository and paper graded at W14. Students who fall behind in these weeks will face compounding debt heading into the W13 final assembly week.

The peer review cycle across W10-W12 is graded independently per week, but the W10 review-response step (Step 3) is graded as part of W12, not W10. This creates an invisible dependency: W12 grading criteria include 'Reviewers' audit of their partner's repo' AND resolution of W10 blocking comments, making W12 the de facto close-out for the entire W10-W12 peer-review arc.

These four weeks are independently graded mini-assignments. W1 establishes the repository infrastructure reused in all subsequent weeks; W2-W4 build test-driven, RAG, and agentic skills used in project weeks. No explicit deliverable file from W1-W4 is required in the W14 final repository, but the repository created in W1 HW Step 1 ('ai-physics-<lastname>') is the same repository used throughout.

The proposal is graded independently at W5. However, it is the gating document for the entire project arc (W6-W14). No deliverable file from W5 is explicitly required in the W14 submission, yet the proposal's research question, dataset, and method directly determine what students build in W6-W13.
